report.summary:
Package crucible/src/crucible/innovation/ implements INTERFACE_CONTRACTS section 7 and the Gate J/L measurements. All 17 workstream-G gate tests pass.

(1) Capability registry, module caps (caps.py). It subclasses the 4.0 Capabilities module under the same name 'caps'.
- New endpoints: caps.declare {service_host, capability:{name, inputs, outputs, doc}, tests_ref?}, caps.search {query} (the 4.0 {q} form unchanged), caps.try {service_host, capability, input}, caps.verify, caps.adopt_service, caps.drop_service, caps.declaration(s), caps.adoptions.
- caps.try runs the real service through the cloud path, so the caller pays, it runs in the sandbox and it is metered.
- caps.verify runs an independent test suite on fresh seeds. Adoption needs a successful caps.try by the adopter first; later calls are counted as use.
- The v5 surface exists only with config {registry: true}, so 4.0/3.0 tool catalogues, digests and logs are unchanged.

(2) Needs graph, module needs (needs.py).
- Five node kinds and six relation types (requires, consumes, produces, constrains, substitutes, complements), read off world state.
- The process needs.update derives needs with rules keyed only by relation type: supply, provide, alternative and complement needs.
- Needs are visible to holders only; operator evidence stays evaluator-side. Holders can publish requests (needs.publish/requests). A need is marked addressed and then resolved.
- special_case_triggers checks every need has a valid relation path.

(3) Software ecosystem, module pkg (pkg.py): register, release (sandbox tests, API extraction, semver compatibility, docs), search/info, transitive dependency locks, upgrade gated by the dependent's own tests, exec/ci with call tracing, deploy, PRs with an independent-review rule, forks, issues, star, yank, and advisories verified by failing reproductions with fixed_in re-checks. Adoption counts only when the package's code ran inside a dependent's own sandboxed run.

(4) Need-driven participants, module adopt (adopt.py). They discover, test on their own generated inputs, adopt, use, recommend on the forum, publish needs and switch to substitutes.

(5) Supporting files:
- infra/worlds.py: innovation_spec and providers.
- formats.py: route.batch.
- reference.py: scripted creators and the software history.
- scenarios.py: market, capacity, batch, social and software, plus fork arms.
- measure.py: Gate J/L helpers.

Measured (latest run):
- Gate J: 4 executable agent products; 24 independent discoverers and 24 users; Fisher p=1.6e-12 for good vs weaker implementation; 1,092 independent sales; +57,694 compute units vs the no-product fork; 2 product categories.
- Gate L: 5 capability effects; 8 emerged needs; 2 needs addressed by new things; 4 chains of at least 4 stages; 3 of 3 counterfactual removals confirming; 0 bonuses.
- SP-6.3: 1 novel service adopted by 24; the useless one was adopted by 0.
- SP-6.4: 6 relation types used; 0 special-case triggers (includes a rename-invariance check).
- SP-6.5: 15 of 15 features; 2 adoptions by execution.

requirements.notes: 4 agent-created executable products: 1 declared service with 1,092 ok requests, and 3 packages. Creators are scripted reference agents acting through tools.
4 published: public caps.declared events (search-indexed) and pkg.released events.
24 independent discoverers. The participants are workstream-G adopters, not the B population.
24 independent users for whom the service actually executed.
Forks of one snapshot: same declaration, good vs weaker code. 24/24 vs 1/24 adopters, Fisher p=1.6e-12.
1,092 sales paid from the own accounts of 24 independent payers.
+57,694 metered compute units and +9,100 cents compute rent vs the no-product fork.
5 effects measured by forks with vs without the agent-created capability.
8 needs emerged after the first update.
2 needs addressed (a substitute service adopted by 32 holders; a fixed package release) and resolved.
4 chains of at least 4 stages, each in its own world and seed (capacity, technology-compute, social, software). The first act of each is scripted.
3 of 3 removal forks confirm the dependency (deterministic cost model, invariants clean).
Novel service discovered, tested on participants' own generated inputs, adopted and used by 24. The useless service was adopted by 0. Independent suite scored 1.00 vs 0.50.
6 relation types used. 0 special-case triggers: path validity, rule literals and rename invariance all checked.
15 of 15 features. 2 adoptions by traced execution.

tests_run.command: PYTHONPATH=src python -m crucible.scale.slots --cpu 2 --gpu-mb 0 -- python -m pytest -q tests/v5/test_gate_SP_6_5.py tests/v5/test_gate_SP_6_3.py tests/v5/test_gate_J.py tests/v5/test_gate_SP_6_4.py tests/v5/test_gate_L.py (CRUCIBLE_V5_AUTHOR=ws-G; final code; 82.7 s)
regression group 0 (20 test files incl. test_diagnostics, test_v5_innovation_caps) via slots --cpu 1, after the caps fix
regression group 1 (20 test files incl. test_scale, test_agents_llm) via slots --cpu 1, run as a background job
regression group 2 (20 test files incl. test_v5_innovation_needs/pkg, test_storage) via slots --cpu 1

limitations: Creators and developers are scripted reference agents (feasibility only, labelled kind=scripted). Participants are rule-based need-driven adopters (crucible.innovation.adopt), not the workstream-B population.
The social channel is the 4.0 forum; workstream-C platforms are not used.

Needs observables cover services, compute instances, declared capabilities and packages only. Content, communities, education, organisations and supply chains are not covered. The complements relation comes only from JSON-schema compatibility or relations supplied as world config.
Objective usefulness is measured only for formats with a verifier (4.0 NEEDS and innovation.formats). Subjective usefulness from diverse participant responses is not implemented.
Package adoption tracing counts Python-level calls into deps/<repo>/ (sys.setprofile); code that only imports a package without calling it does not count as adoption.
Exact counterfactual forks require cost_model deterministic (innovation_spec sets it). Exact metric values shift slightly between commits because adding events changes the seq-keyed rng.
The v5 registry is opt-in per world (caps config registry: true).

Regression group 1's test_scale::test_keyboard_interrupt_leaves_no_process_behind timed out only because SIGINT is ignored in background shell jobs. It passes in the foreground and was failing identically before any caps fix; it is not related to this work.
integration_notes: Workstream A's substrate was not merged during this work (git merge of feat/crucible-5-openworld was already up to date at the end). Nothing in crucible.substrate is used: packages are 4.0 code repositories, sandbox outcomes are recorded through ctx.reserve/fill, and cross-module effects use 4.0 hooks (on_service_call, needs_demand) instead of bus.subscribe.

caps.py registers a subclass of the 4.0 Capabilities module under the same module name 'caps'; MODULES['caps'] is replaced when crucible.innovation.modules is imported. Without config registry:true the v5 endpoints are withdrawn at install and caps.search keeps its 4.0 schema, so tool catalogues and digests are unchanged. The 3.0 catalogue check in tests/test_diagnostics.py and the 3.0 byte-identity tests pass.

To use the v5 mechanisms in a world, add {'name':'caps','config':{'registry':true}}, 'needs' and 'pkg' (pkg depends on identity, bank, code, issues). 'adopt' (participants) and 'infra' (providers) are optional. innovation.worlds.innovation_spec builds such a world.

Population (B): world.hooks['needs_demand'](world) -> [(principal, capability, schema)] declares individuals' task needs. Individuals acting through caps.search/try/adopt_service are counted by innovation.measure unchanged.

Civilizations (J): the needs module config 'interfaces' and 'edges' add couplings as data. Chain and counterfactual helpers are innovation.measure.Stage/chain_record/counterfactual and innovation.scenarios.arms.
Primitives (A 1.5): pkg adds package, release and dependency records over 4.0 code repositories (the software_repository owner) and declares no second repository table.
Evidence files produced while testing were deleted and not committed. A tracked docs/v5/evidence/checker_report.json rewritten by the regression run was restored to HEAD.
The pyproject.toml extra was not needed: no packages were installed.
measurements: Gate J: products 4; independent discoverers 24; independent users 24; adoption p=1.6e-12 (24/24 vs 1/24); independent transactions 1,092 (3,276 cents, 24 payers); compute delta +57,694 CU and +9,100 cents rent; product categories 2

Gate L: effects 5; emerged needs 8; needs addressed by new services 2 (32+1 holders adopting); chains 4 with at least 4 stages; counterfactual confirmations 3/3 (capacity 1 vs 0 supply needs and 63 vs 0 later adoptions; batch 4.60M vs 3.09M base CU and 105 vs 0 overloads; social 12 vs 1 forum adopters); special-case bonuses 0
SP-6.3: 1 novel service fully discovered, tested, adopted and used by 24; useless service tested by 24, adopted by 0; independent verification 1.00 vs 0.50
SP-6.4: 6 relation types used; special-case triggers 0 (0 invalid paths, 0 rule literals naming entities, 0 rename-invariance differences); 8 emergences
SP-6.5: 15/15 features; 2 adoptions by execution (one transitive); 1 star, not counted
Speed: 20 participants for 3 simulated days take about 2 s; market scenario with 3 arms about 8 s; 36-participant capacity world for 7 days about 10 s per arm; all 17 gate tests 83 s

files_changed_outside_owned_paths.why: The brief assigns these gate test files to workstream G.
Unit and integration tests, named per contract rule 0.7 (tests/test_v5_<area>_*.py).
